# Five-format legacy comparison

Task6 references all ten legacy answer goldens (full/minimal × five formats). The other six legacy files are menu/aux/ESXi evidence owned by Tasks7/8, not changed by this task. New fixtures are handwritten model.Snapshot input independent of builtin templates, as approved; actual builtin defaults and hook fragments are Task9. BIOS/UEFI are separate in all twenty fixtures.

`legacy-line-diff.md` enumerates every deleted/inserted line with old/new one-based line numbers and exact range reasons. `decoded-scaffolds.md` decodes every encoded command in all twenty fixtures so scripts remain reviewable. No hash substitutes for payload inspection. Categories: S1–S5 are expected structural/input ownership changes; B1–B4 are intentional lifecycle/syntax/regression fixes. There are zero unresolved changes.

The renderer now consumes template/fragment content rather than reassembling a fixed old model. Locale, partitions, identity, network and package profile fields survive when authored in the snapshot. These independent fixtures deliberately use /dev/sda, task-42, shorter valid credential strings and no default SSH key injection. Full/minimal differs in actual per-timing instances, not one-off old serializer flags. Missing old default credentials/packages/NIC settings are not assertions that builtin profiles may omit them: Task9 must implement real defaults and SSH hook.

Legacy inline shell functions/global exports are replaced by one-line decoded scaffold commands which download FileScript wrappers through canonical gateway AnswerURL. Hook bodies are fetched by digest from the gateway, not an invented artifacts/hooks filesystem. Task8 owns wrapper correctness (timeout/digest/EnvName/per-instance required/optional/log reporting). Firstboot staging and the real systemd native runner are implemented here; hook execution waits until reboot and uses local finalize.token. Required wrapper failure stops native cleanup. Cleanup clears cached credentials/payloads only after success. Telemetry transport failure remains nonfatal.

Kickstart corrections explicitly pin Appendix A 743e8af (url source), 9a252db (cmdline), 2d59bbb (%include after %pre) and 83584d7 (BIOS GPT biosboot / UEFI ESP). Preseed a570ad5 is also pinned by safe single-line replacement and decoded POSIX syntax checks. Handwritten kickstart writes the real firmware-specific partition fragment into the include file in pre before use, so the regression verifies a real include dataflow.

Windows uses one native oobeSystem FirstLogonCommand source chain; separate commands are concurrent in modern Windows. Each local wrapper must read finalize token itself, so no shared-process environment assumption. Compact -File firstboot.ps1/cleanup.ps1 invocations replace whole encoded programs to honor the native 1,024-character CommandLine maximum: all four one-slot fixtures are 304 decoded characters; eight slots also fit. Author source text/slot counts must obey this native field limit; XML parsing alone does not validate native schema. The actual UTF8-BOM PS script bytes are produced by windowsPartScript and pinned by two separate .ps1.golden files; decoded evidence shows these concrete staged files. WinPE pre wrappers are separate injected files and do not execute firstboot. FileAux must stage wrappers/hooks/token AND those two PS files through official setup /m OEM copying before reboot. Actual login/AutoLogon prerequisite, Server-only scope and target-volume copying require Task9/Task7 real machine validation. No fabricated password or installer PowerShell.

Author placement and cross-task contract is in the task report and `task-6-runtime-contract.md`. Primary sources checked 2026-10-11:

- Subiquity early/late shell commands, /target, command failure: https://canonical-subiquity.readthedocs-hosted.com/en/latest/reference/autoinstall-reference.html
- AutoYaST pre/chroot scripts and /mnt: https://documentation.suse.com/sles/15-SP7/single-html/SLES-autoyast/book-autoyast.html
- Windows FirstLogon concurrency: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/unattend/microsoft-windows-shell-setup-firstlogoncommands-synchronouscommand-order
